findings.title: Retire obsolete two-transport simulator
findings.why_it_matters: The declared interview simulation now asserts a 200 fallback flip and then submits typed answers through the retired transport. The changed route always returns 409, so the release/E2E harness fails before it can validate the real-time reconnect and grading path the patch is meant to protect.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace simulateRealtimeDegradation with a realtime-only reconnect scenario: assert /fallback refuses the stale request, retain the realtime transport, append resumed agent/student turns through the agent endpoints, call agent-complete with finished:true, and run the grading assertion. Delete the post-fallback nextQuestion/submitAnswer loop and update the script header/docs to describe one transport.

findings.title: Remove duplicated source-inspection tests
findings.why_it_matters: The same production conditions are asserted twice in separate test styles, multiplying the maintenance surface without covering another behavior. The source-file reads also produced ResourceWarnings in the targeted unittest run, so this duplicate test surface is both noisy and brittle.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep ProductionInterviewSafetyTests as the single regression location, replace its open(...).read() calls with Path('main.py').read_text(encoding='utf-8'), and delete the duplicate TestVoiceFailover and TestReconnectSafety methods.

findings.title: Delete dead text-answer compatibility shim
findings.why_it_matters: The route explicitly retains a false-valued export only for callers/tests, but the repository has no application caller. Keeping a named permission function after removing the capability makes the retired manual path look supported and invites future code to branch on an API that can never enable behavior.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete textAnswersAllowed and its environment-matrix assertion in interview-session.test.ts. Keep the endpoint-level 410 test, which directly protects the real contract for stale manual clients.
evidence: lms/app/api/interview/answer/route.ts:8: /** Retained for callers/tests; manual text answers are never accepted now. */

findings.title: Remove stale fallback terminology
findings.why_it_matters: The changed parent now reconnects to the LiveKit room, but child component comments and the callback name still describe flipping to the deleted turn-based transport. This is comment and sibling-path drift: a later maintainer can reasonably restore or test the wrong failure policy from these local contracts.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename onFallback and fallbackRef to onReconnect/reconnectRef through RealtimeRoom and MeetingView, then replace stale turn-based fallback comments in those files and realtime.ts with the real-time reconnect policy. Update only related build documentation that still declares two student transports.

residual_risks: The real-time admission health check proves an agent heartbeat and source SHA, not that a worker can accept and speak in a newly minted LiveKit room; only a live canary can establish that end-to-end property.
The agent now stays alive after participant disconnect, but this review did not execute the LiveKit SDK lifecycle to confirm a reconnect preserves the expected audio subscriptions and agent state.
Egress quota exhaustion remains an external recording dependency; the scoped diff does not make a successful graded completion contingent on a usable recording artifact.
testing_gaps: No executable browser test drives LiveKitRoom disconnect -> token remint -> RealtimeRoom remount and asserts the same interviewId, live transport, and continued turn persistence.
The new Python regression tests inspect source strings rather than invoking an AgentSession with an AgentHandoff event or a participant disconnect, so SDK API compatibility is not exercised.

No current suite validates a real LLM-student transcript through the deployed agent, agent-complete, queued worker grading, and the result page; the existing package simulation instead targets the removed fallback path.
